Topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

Target audience: University students (Computer Science/AI minor)

Section: section_1 — The Analogy: Library vs. Book Content

Lecture lines:
Attention mechanisms act like a library's index catalog.
MLP layers store the actual knowledge contents.
Like books, MLPs hold the facts within.

Planned animations:
Create a library icon in light blue (#ADD8E6) and a book icon in white (#FFFFFF) in center.
Show book icon moving into library icon, emphasizing categorization.
Highlight the library icon with yellow (#FFFF00) to represent the MLP structure.

Section: section_2 — The MLP Mechanism: Key-Value Memories

Lecture lines:
Input vector activates a specific key.
Neurons act like locks for specific patterns.
Matching keys trigger value outputs.

Planned animations:
Display MLP layers as a sequence of rectangles in light blue (#ADD8E6).
Highlight individual weights as small nodes within layers using green (#00FF00).
Animate signal flowing through nodes as arrows in white (#FFFFFF).

Section: section_3 — Visualizing Weights as Knowledge

Lecture lines:
Facts aren't single nodes, but constellations.
Activation lights up a specific neural path.
This forms the knowledge representation pattern.
Spotlight effect shows fact distribution clearly.
Connections define the stored relational truth.

Planned animations:
Visualize a single weight vector in light cyan (#E0FFFF) pointing to an output.
Flash the vector with gold (#FFD700) to represent 'active' knowledge extraction.
Label the vector 'Learned Knowledge' in white (#FFFFFF) above it.

Section: section_4 — The Memory Retrieval Process

Lecture lines:
Inputs activate dedicated fact neurons.
Information projects to output space.
Weights allow surgical model editing.

Planned animations:
Display input token represented by a pulsing light blue (#ADD8E6) circle.
Show the circle passing through layers, transforming color to gold (#FFD700).
Display retrieved output concept emerging from the final layer.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion and Limitations

Lecture lines:
MLPs function as compressed, fuzzy databases.
Knowledge is associative, not rigid.
Connected weights allow robust inference.

Planned animations:
Show the MLP model fading from view in dark gray (#A9A9A9).
Display 'Storage Capacity' limitations text in light red (#FFC0CB).
Final summary text appears in white (#FFFFFF) indicating key takeaways.
